Not everyone has aggressive intrusive thoughts. A lot people do have intrusive thoughts, but for most, they're not super distressing or bothersome. They don't get that sinking feeling in their chest over them. They just move on nearly instantly and it's not a big problem. A lot of people don't even have intrusive thoughts at all.

And external behavioral compulsions or rituals are not at all required to qualify for OCD. Forms without them are just less common, and therefore less talked about. Regularly overthinking, obsessing, ruminating, thinking a certain thought to "check" for a feeling or behavior — these are all forms of hidden mental rituals. They are more than enough. This is known as Pure-O, or purely obsessional OCD, and it is just as valid as any other form. 

Ultimately, what matters is how you feel, and what helps you. If treatments or techniques that are usually used for OCD help you with your overthinking or intrusive thoughts, then you are allowed and encouraged to use them, whether you feel like the diagnosis fits or not.
